member.summary: SensorStatus will return the all the sensor settings inside the printer.
member.value: A string of all the sensor values in the printer in ABC=0;DEF=1; etc.

remarks.para: For HDP6600: The string is composed of two parts: an identifier telling what the sensor is and a value indicating its state. For most sensor's it is a 1 for closed and 0 for open. Some sensors have multiple states. More information about available sensors and their values can be found in the section.

Some Sensors have other settings needed to fully utilize their functionality. HFS Reports the current card sensor status and HVP reports the current hopper position. If the current HVP does not indicate eHOPPER_IS_DOWN then HFS will not return valid information. If you want to check for cards at anytime, you need to turn off exception feed. This can be done by going to (MENU->Setup Printer->Hopper Settings->Exception Feed) and setting it to Off. This causes the hopper to stay in the dropped position at all times other than printing. When a card is being printed, the hopper will stay in the raised position until about 2 seconds after the card is ejected.

member.name: P:Fargo.PrinterSDK.PrinterInfo.SerialNumber
member.summary: Gets the printer's serial number.
member.value: The printer's serial number.

remarks.para:
The serial number is composed of two parts: a code representing the time the printer was built and a sequence number to ensure that all serial numbers are unique. The precise format of the number is as follows:
Character(s) Meaning
1 Letter (A-Z) representing the decade, starting from the year 2000 (i.e., "A"=2000, "B"=2010, etc).
2 Digit (0-9) representing the year.
3-4 Two digits representing the week in which the printer was built.
5-8 Sequence number (unique among all printers built that week).
For example, the serial number A5250018 represents a printer built during the 25th week of 2005 (A-5-25), with sequence number 0018.
